g.text: What the judge found in each model's rewrites

text.style: font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #172b42
font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #526379

g.text: Each bar splits the key points of every rewrite the judge read: kept in full; partly kept, when a condition, exception, or limiting word such as may or only is lost or blurred; left out; or

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #526379

g.text: contradicted, when the rewrite says something the passage rules out.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #526379

g.text: Critical key points are the ones a reader would be misled by losing. A rewrite could mislead when it contradicts a critical point or adds a major claim the passage does not make.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #526379

g.text: Judge: claude-opus-5-5, in six fresh Claude Code subagent sessions of six or seven passages each, mixing both passage sets, blind to which model wrote each rewrite, against the key points in

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #526379
